analysis.title: Energy, Utilities & Mining Pulse: Investors Asking: Where to Seek Absolute and Relative Defense Amid Natural Resources?
key_insights: With the S&P down 6% week-to-date, GS Portfolio Strategists keep a constructive 2027 view but say investors should also own some relative defense against downside tails from AI, elections and the Middle East conflict. The Natural Resources team picks one stock per sub-sector for that purpose.

Utilities: GS picks Duke Energy (DUK, Buy, $145 PT, 14% total return) as the defensive utility. North Carolina had no gubernatorial election this year, the NC rate case settlements were approved, Duke is fully regulated and has no Texas exposure.
GS expects Duke management to raise its earnings growth outlook and the capital plan on the 4Q26 call. GS estimates are 2%/3%/5% above FactSet consensus in 2027/2028/2029.

Midstream: GS sees contracted gas demand growth as the most defensive midstream theme. Sanctioned backlogs are ~14-15% of 2026 EV across coverage, and almost all 2026-28 incremental EBITDA growth is already sanctioned. Valuations are high versus history.

TC Energy (TRP, Buy, US$73 / C$102 PT) has the most direct gas transmission exposure in coverage (~89% of 2032E EBITDA vs 73% at DTM, 67% at KMI, 31% at WMB). In 3Q26 it sanctioned the $1.8b Crossroads project, extended its 5-7% EBITDA CAGR through 2031 and raised its origination shadow backlog to C$40b.

US Majors: GS favors integrated oils for diversification with minimal AI exposure, because upstream plus downstream gives a margin buffer across the cycle. Chevron (CVX, Buy, $245 PT) is the expression. It plans to divest HESM and DJ Basin crude midstream assets by year-end and guides to $2.5-$3bn of buybacks next quarter.

E&P: Liquids-weighted E&Ps have outperformed gas E&Ps year-to-date (+33% vs -5%). GS sees gas E&Ps as the most defensive pocket because gas sentiment is already weak. The FY2027 Henry Hub forward ($3.08) sits below GS's $3.50 mid-cycle view.

GS attributes the soft gas outlook to one structural factor (2027 winter US supply growth topping demand growth on Permian pipeline capacity) and one speculative factor (El Niño). GS Commodities sees only a weak correlation between Niño intensity and winter temperature deviations.

EQT (Buy, $62 PT, 22% upside) is the gas E&P pick. It is low-cost with deep Appalachian inventory, ~12 Bcf/d capacity (~17 Bcf/d pro forma with RRC), supply deals with power and LNG buyers, and can curtail volumes into weak prices and ramp quickly into strong ones.

Energy Services: GS prefers geographically diversified, long-cycle exposure, which it views as lower beta to commodity prices. SLB ($63 PT) is highlighted as the largest OFS company by revenue, positive into 2027 on energy security investment by NOCs and IOCs in Latin America, Africa and the Middle East.

Metals & Mining: Nucor (NUE, $335 PT) is the defensive pick on balance sheet and free cash flow. Net debt was ~0.5x at 3Q26 and GS forecasts ~0.1x by end-2027. GS forecasts capital returns of $1.98bn in 2026 rising 36% to $2.7bn in 2027, about 5% of market cap.

Clean Tech: GS sees utility-scale solar and storage as relatively defensive, backed by ~86 GW of US data-center capacity under construction. Nextpower (NXT, Buy on Conviction List, $127 PT) is the pick. Its Capital Markets Day set a >$7.5bn FY2030 revenue target (>20% CAGR from ~$4.3bn in FY2027) and >$8.00 EPS.
Near-term risk flagged for solar is that the Section 232 polysilicon outcome could pause contracting as PPAs reprice. GS says the midterm result lowered policy risk for the sector.

Investor feedback on E&Ps: DVN debate centers on the post-merger portfolio review and divestitures (Anadarko kept), with >$1.0bn of 4Q26 buybacks and ~$6.3bn of 2027E excess FCF. OVV questions center on M&A appetite, Canada after the BC elections and cash tax savings from a proposed deduction.

Refining: investor interest in PSX and MPC followed softer 2027 crack spreads. Bulls on PSX cite diversified earnings and debt targets, bears cite chemicals margins and Western Gateway execution. Bears on MPC see full valuation and estimate risk if margins soften further.

Canadian oils: CNQ will buy Advantage Energy (AAV) for C$2.53bn cash (~79 MBOE/d of Montney and Charlie Lake output). Investors see consolidation accelerating (CVE/MEG, TVE/HWX, CVE/ATH, SHEL/ARX), and Alberta's new royalty program is supportive.

Energy Services: HAL inbounds focus on 2027 revision magnitude, US completions pricing increases and Argentina activity. HP's FY2027 international rig guide of 50-60 is below GS, while 1FQ27 international direct margin guidance of $35-55mm is in line.

Midstream: Barnett/Woodford is the new Permian volume theme. Diamondback sees ~50% higher 12-month cumulative oil than core Midland benches, and EPD cited GORs of 8-9x against ~2x in Wolfcamp. TRGP is named as having unmodeled Barnett upside.

Alberta's Oil Sands Growth Program sets a 2% royalty for the first five years for projects announced after Nov. 15, rising to 6% by years nine and ten. Investors question whether this alone unlocks shipper commitments for ENB's MLO2 and Pacific Link, and note a December 2029 review.

Utilities: Texas-exposed names are on hold until the legislative session clarifies data-center rules and 765kV transmission. IPP sentiment is muted after a sharp three-month pullback. Talen and CEG draw interest for lower Texas exposure, NRG could have a year-end catalyst if its 1.2 GW data-center contract closes, and VST is expected to stay range-bound.

Regulated utilities: investors are less constructive on SRE, AEP, SO and EXC on regulatory uncertainty and more constructive on DUK, AEE and XEL. Rising rates (10-year at 4.9%) have been a headwind and XLU is underperforming SPY this year.

Metals: steel screens as relatively inexpensive after tariff-driven YTD strength cooled post-midterms. Copper is hurt by an unwind of the AI trade, with COMEX copper down ~14% month-to-date and FCX down ~25%. Gold faces headwinds from rate-increase and inflation concerns.

earnings_insights: TRP 3Q26 (reported): sanctioned the $1.8b Crossroads project, extended its 5-7% EBITDA CAGR through 2031 (low end supported by sanctioned projects), origination shadow backlog raised to C$40b (~C$25b pre-FID gas, ~C$15b pre-FID power).

NUE 3Q26 (reported): net debt ~0.5x, returned ~$629mn to shareholders (~$1.4B YTD), committed to at least 40% of annual net earnings (~42% YTD). GS forecast: $1.98bn returned in 2026 and $2.7bn in 2027, net leverage ~0.1x at end-2027.
DUK: GS expects management to raise its earnings growth outlook and capital plan on the 4Q26 call (GS forecast). GS estimates are 2%/3%/5% above FactSet consensus in 2027/2028/2029.

HP 4FQ26 (reported Nov 18): higher international direct margins. FY2027 average international rig guide of 50-60 is below the GS estimate, and 1FQ27 international direct margin guide of $35-55mm is in line with GS.
Golar LNG 3Q26 (reported): listed in GS research as above consensus, with boat five development starting and boat four commercialization quieter.
CVX: guiding to $2.5-$3bn of buybacks next quarter (company guidance). GS expects Bakken production held at ~180 kbd, moving from three to two rigs and long laterals from 60% to over 85% next year.
DVN: management pointed to >$1.0bn of buybacks in 4Q26 and ~$6.3bn of excess FCF in 2027E (company statements), with preliminary 2027 capex of ~$5.3bn plus Solitude pipeline contributions.

NXT Capital Markets Day: FY2030 revenue target >$7.5bn (>20% CAGR from ~$4.3bn expected in FY2027) and >$8.00 EPS, high-teens adjusted EBITDA margin in FY2028 and a path back to >21% by FY2030 (company targets).
EPD raised its Permian gas and NGL volume outlook on 3Q26 and cited GORs of 8-9x in Woodford/Barnett zones. Diamondback agreed to acquire Double Eagle assets (~$5B per GS research title).
CNQ announced the C$2.53bn cash acquisition of AAV at C$13.55/sh, adding ~79 MBOE/d of production and returning 100% of free cash flow to shareholders.

trade_ideas.description: Long DUK (Buy, $145 12-month PT) as a regulated-utility defensive expression
trade_ideas.rationale: Regulatory overhang removed in North Carolina, fully regulated, no Texas exposure, with an expected raise to the earnings growth outlook on the 4Q26 call.
trade_ideas.risk: DUK's balance sheet not improving, regulatory uncertainty from the recently filed rate case, and any decline in the load growth forecast.

trade_ideas.description: Long TRP (Buy, US$73 / C$102 12-month PT) as a gas midstream defensive expression
trade_ideas.rationale: Most direct gas transmission exposure in coverage with sanctioned growth and relatively favorable Canadian regulation.
trade_ideas.risk: Softer gas or power project execution, higher regulatory hurdles, slower deleveraging, higher capex, and counterparty concentration on Mexico transmission assets.

trade_ideas.description: Long CVX (Buy, $245 12-month PT) as the integrated oil defensive expression
trade_ideas.rationale: Upstream and downstream margin buffer, strong balance sheet and steady buybacks with minimal AI exposure.
trade_ideas.risk: Commodity prices, refining margins and operational execution.

trade_ideas.description: Long EQT (Buy, $62 12-month PT) as the gas E&P defensive expression
trade_ideas.rationale: Low-cost Appalachian production, ability to flex volumes and positive risk/reward skew given weak gas sentiment.
trade_ideas.risk: Lower commodity prices, particularly natural gas, pipeline build-out delays, higher costs, government pronouncements and less favorable well results.

trade_ideas.description: Long SLB ($63 12-month PT) as the oilfield services defensive expression
trade_ideas.rationale: Diversified regional and long-cycle project exposure carries lower beta to commodity prices.
trade_ideas.risk: Commodity prices, slower digital adoption, and a relative pickup in North America versus international activity.

trade_ideas.description: Long NUE ($335 12-month PT) as the metals and mining defensive expression
trade_ideas.rationale: Low leverage, a shift from heavy capex to free cash flow harvest and rising capital returns provide downside support with upside to steel fundamentals.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher scrap costs, lower tariffs, added domestic capacity pressuring prices, and slower economic growth reducing steel demand.

trade_ideas.description: Long NXT (Buy on Conviction List, $127 12-month PT) as the utility-scale solar and storage defensive expression
trade_ideas.rationale: Expansion beyond trackers into storage increases wallet share per project and should let NXT outgrow the solar market.
trade_ideas.risk: Increasing competition, customer attrition, patent protection, market demand, policy, and supplier product availability or pricing.

risk_factors: AI, election and Middle East uncertainty creating downside tail risk for the broader market.
Rising rates, with the 10-year at 4.9%, weigh on utility multiples and commodity performance.
Texas legislative outcomes on data-center development and 765kV transmission affect IPPs and Texas-exposed utilities.
Soft US natural gas pricing from supply growth and El Niño sentiment, plus a possible near-term pause in solar contracting after Section 232.
Softening 2027 refining crack spreads pose estimate risk for refiners.
Derivative unwind of the AI trade and data-center spending caution weigh on copper and FCX.
Tariff expectations normalizing, and seasonal construction slowdown for steel.
Durability of Alberta fiscal terms given the December 2029 review versus multi-decade oil sands project lives.
